1: Figure 1. Overview of adaptive sparse multi-view stable paired differential detection (AS-MVSPD). (A) Alignment of paired measurements across individuals and omics views. (B) Shared individual-level sign flips for joint testing and separate feature-level analysis. IUT denotes the intersection–union test. maxT denotes adjustment based on the maximum feature statistic. (C) Bounded feature scores under consistent, isolated, and opposing paired changes. Pre and Post denote measurements before and after exposure or intervention. KO denotes Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes orthology.
2: Figure 2. Joint power and feature-level error rates in simulations. (A) Joint rejection at  n=8 with signals in zero to three views. Signals in fewer than three views represent the joint null. Signals in all three views represent the alternative. (B, C) Joint power across signal counts at  n=8 and 12, respectively. (D) Feature-level family-wise error rate (FWER) after maximum-statistic adjustment (maxT) under five sign-symmetric settings. (E) Joint power under first-order autoregressive (AR (1)) and block correlation at n=8 and 12. (F) Feature-level FWER under Tukey-g asymmetry at n=8 with zero, five, or 20 signals. Each configuration used 500 replicates. Error bars in A–C and E indicate 95% Wilson intervals. D and F show point estimates. Horizontal dashed lines in A–D and F mark 0.050. AS-MVSPD denotes adaptive sparse multi-view stable paired differential detection. The paired comparators use adaptive sum of powered score (aSPU), Chen–Qin-type (CQ), and RankCOM-type rank-based statistics with intersection–union testing (IUT). Labels without the Paired prefix denote the same comparators. CLR denotes centered log-ratio transformation. t3 denotes Student’s t distribution with three degrees of freedom. n denotes the number of paired individuals.
3: Figure 3. Joint testing in four public paired microbiome–metabolome subsets. (A) Numbers of paired individuals and features. (B) View-specific and joint P-values. (C) Joint P-values from four methods. (D) Proportions of significant AS-MVSPD joint tests after individual deletion or sampling 80% of features without replacement within each view. Labels report significant tests over total tests. Significance was defined as P ≤ 0.050. Dashed lines in B and C mark P = 0.050. Analyses used all 256 sign patterns for HADDAD and prespecified closed subgroups of 256 patterns for MARS and HE infants. HE infants denotes the 2- to 12-month comparison in 57 infants. P-values are unadjusted for testing multiple study subsets. AS-MVSPD denotes adaptive sparse multi-view stable paired differential detection. Paired-aSPU-IUT, Paired-CQ-IUT, and Paired-RankCOM-IUT denote paired comparators using adaptive sum of powered score, Chen–Qin-type, and RankCOM-type rank-based statistics with intersection–union testing (IUT). IHH denotes intermittent hypoxia and hypercapnia. IBS denotes irritable bowel syndrome. n denotes the number of paired individuals.
4: Figure 4. Paired multi-omics analysis of eight rats before and after hyperbaric exposure. (A) Study design and feature counts. (B) View-specific and joint P-values. (C) Selected species, orthology features, and six representative metabolite features with maxT-adjusted P < 0.050. Score signs indicate mean paired-change directions. (D) Paired differences for features in C, divided by each feature’s standard deviation across rats. Red and blue indicate positive and negative changes. Color intensity indicates scaled magnitude. (E) Representative paired measurements on the indicated analysis scales. Lines connect measurements from the same rat. Blue and red denote measurements before (Pre) and after (Post) exposure in A and E. (F) Proportions of selected features increasing or decreasing, indicated by dark and light shades. Green, purple, and orange identify species, orthology, and metabolite data. KO denotes Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes orthology. IUT denotes intersection–union test. maxT denotes adjustment based on the maximum feature statistic. CLR denotes centered log-ratio transformation. ppm denotes parts per million.
S1: Supplementary Figure S1. Data processing and quality control. (A) Matching of samples before (Pre) and after (Post) exposure in eight rats. Species and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes Orthology (KO) features came from the same metagenomic sample pairs. (B) Feature counts after filtering and annotation. (C) Mean paired changes on each view's analysis scale, restricted to the 1st–99th percentiles for display. Magnitudes are not directly comparable across analysis scales. (D) Annotation scores and quality-control (QC) coefficients of variation (CVs) for untargeted metabolite features. Dashed lines mark 0.8 and 30%. (E) Median absolute paired change after standard-deviation scaling for each rat. (F) Final matrix dimensions and transformations.
S2: Supplementary Figure S2. Core two-view simulations. Empirical rejection rates are shown for the global null, stable sparse signals, stable signals with an outlying individual, an outlying individual alone, signals in one view alone, and mixed paired-change directions. Each configuration included 500 replicates. Error bars show 95% Wilson intervals.
S3: Supplementary Figure S3. Signal settings, sensitivity analyses, and runtime. (A–C) Power across effect sizes, signal counts per view, and shared latent-loading scales. Each configuration included 500 replicates. Error bars show 95% Wilson intervals. (D) Joint P-values across 20 closed-subgroup seeds for MARS and HE infants. Full-group results for HADDAD Air and IHH provide references. (E) Frequencies of selected top-k scales pooled across both views over 30 independent subsamples containing 80% of features per view. HE denotes the 57-infant comparison between 2 and 12 months. (F) Single-threaded runtime for three views across sample sizes, feature counts, and sign-pattern counts. Points show medians of five timings, and error bars show interquartile ranges. IHH denotes intermittent hypoxia and hypercapnia. In D, black horizontal bars mark medians, and the dashed line marks P = 0.05.
S4: Supplementary Figure S4. Sensitivity analyses in public paired data. (A) Joint P-values after deletion of one paired individual at a time, with HE analysis-ready features locked. (B) Joint P-values from 30 subsamples containing 80% of features selected without replacement within each view. (C) Joint P-values under 20 additional seeds for 256-element closed sign subgroups in MARS and HE infants. HADDAD Air and IHH full-group results provide reference points. Dashed lines mark P = 0.05. HE denotes 57 infants paired at 2 and 12 months. IHH denotes intermittent hypoxia and hypercapnia. Black horizontal bars mark medians.
S5: Supplementary Figure S5. Feature-level results in eight rats. (A) Ranked self-normalized scores. (B) Counts of increasing and decreasing features with maxT-adjusted P < 0.05. Negative bars represent decreases. (C) Mean scores at each top-k scale. Circles mark scales selected by calibrated adaptive evidence. (D) Cohen's dz after deletion of each rat for four species and three Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes Orthology (KO) features. The horizontal axis identifies the omitted rat. (E) Paired changes for 78 metabolite features with maxT-adjusted P < 0.05, ordered by observed self-normalized score. Differences after minus before exposure are divided by the feature-specific standard deviation across rats. (F) MaxT-adjusted P-values for 1,029 metabolite features. M118T213_pos, putatively annotated as betaine, ranks 344th with maxT-adjusted P = 0.617188. MaxT denotes adjustment based on the maximum feature statistic.
S6: Supplementary Figure S6. Structured-correlation simulations. (A) Joint rejection rates with stable signals in two of three views. (B) Joint power with five stable signals in every view. (C) Power at n = 12 for AS-MVSPD and paired aSPU-type, Chen–Qin-type, and RankCOM-type comparators. Solid and dashed lines indicate first-order autoregressive (AR(1)) and block correlation, respectively. (D) Family-wise error rates (FWER) after maximum-statistic adjustment (maxT) among true-null features in prespecified view 1. Each view contained 100 unit-variance features. Corresponding features had cross-view correlation 0.3, and within-view correlation was ρ ∈ {0, 0.3, 0.7, 0.9}. Each configuration included 500 replicates. Error bars show 95% Wilson intervals. AS-MVSPD denotes adaptive sparse multi-view stable paired differential detection. aSPU denotes adaptive sum of powered score.
S7: Supplementary Figure S7. Tukey-g asymmetry stress test. (A) Joint false-rejection rates at n = 8 with signals in zero of three views. (B) Joint false-rejection rates at n = 8 with five stable signals in two of three views. (C) Joint false-rejection rates under the two-of-three-view configuration at n = 12. (D) Joint power at n = 12 with five stable signals in every view. Panels A–D compare AS-MVSPD with paired aSPU-type, Chen–Qin-type, and RankCOM-type tests. g = 0 represents normal noise, and larger g represents greater right skew. Each configuration included 500 replicates. Error bars show 95% Wilson intervals. AS-MVSPD denotes adaptive sparse multi-view stable paired differential detection. aSPU denotes adaptive sum of powered score. Feature-level family-wise error rates after maximum-statistic adjustment appear in Fig. 2F.
S8: Supplementary Figure S8. Leave-one-individual-out (LOO) ablation under individual contamination. Spearman correlations compare feature rankings before and after deletion of the contaminated individual for AS-MVSPD and AS-MVSPD+LOO at contamination magnitudes of 4, 8, and 12. Each magnitude included 250 simulations. View-specific correlations were averaged across three views within each simulation. Points show means across 250 simulations. Error bars show 95% percentile bootstrap intervals from 10,000 resamples of the replicate means using seed 20260803. AS-MVSPD denotes adaptive sparse multi-view stable paired differential detection. AS-MVSPD+LOO includes the additional individual-deletion constraint.
S9: Supplementary Figure S9. Adaptive and fixed top-k tests. (A, B) Joint power with signals in both views at effect sizes 1.1 and 1.4, respectively. (C, D) Joint false-rejection rates at effect sizes 1.1 and 1.4 with signals in the first view alone. The horizontal axis shows one, five, or 20 signals per signal-bearing view at equally spaced positions. Each configuration included 12 paired individuals, 200 features per view, and 500 simulations. Methods used identical simulated datasets and the same prespecified 256-element closed sign subgroup. Points show rejection rates, and error bars show 95% Wilson intervals. Horizontal offsets separate method markers without changing signal counts. Dashed lines in C and D mark α = 0.05. Supplementary Table S10 includes global-null results. Supplementary Methods S1.6 describes generation and calibration. AS-MVSPD denotes adaptive sparse multi-view stable paired differential detection.
S10: Supplementary Figure S10. HE infant application and checks. (A) Complete-pair retention in the original feeding groups. (B) Fixed comparison of 2 and 12 months. (C) Longitudinal tests within each original feeding group, with preprocessing repeated within group. (D) Selected transformations and detection thresholds. P-values use 256-element closed subgroups and are not adjusted across sensitivity analyses or feeding groups. The 4,096-pattern audit gave joint P < 0.001. Detailed results are supplied in Supplementary Table S11. These analyses assess developmental and dietary changes and do not identify between-group treatment effects or verify sign invariance. Dark and light segments in A denote included and excluded infants, respectively. Dashed lines in C and D mark P = 0.05.
